sections.h2: Where is Wood County, Ohio, and who bills its property tax?
sections.html:
Wood County lies in northwest Ohio, just south of Lucas County, with Bowling Green as county seat and largest city. The Maumee River forms its diagonal northwest edge, and the county neighbors Lucas, Ottawa, Sandusky, Seneca, Hancock, Putnam and Henry counties. It is part of the Toledo metropolitan area and covers about 617 square miles of land.

Cities in the county are Bowling Green, Northwood, Perrysburg and Rossford, plus a small piece of Fostoria. Perrysburg was the first county seat, and the seat moved to Bowling Green in 1870. School districts that send bills include Bowling Green City, Perrysburg Exempted Village, Rossford Exempted Village, Anthony Wayne, Eastwood, Elmwood, Lake, Lakota, McComb, North Baltimore, Northwood, Otsego, Patrick Henry, Gibsonburg and Fostoria. The Auditor sets values and the Treasurer collects the money, and both offices are on One Courthouse Square in Bowling Green. The county courthouse itself broke ground on November 28, 1893, after citizens chose to move the seat from Perrysburg.

sections.h2: What do Census figures show for Wood County homes?
sections.html:
QuickFacts puts the July 2025 population of Wood County at 134,176, up 1.5 percent from the 2020 base, with 54,257 households in the 2020 to 2024 survey. Owners occupy 64.4 percent of homes, which leaves roughly a third of households renting. The Census Bureau counts 5,955 veterans in the county for 2020 to 2024, a group the Auditor's disabled veteran program is written for.

  • Median value of an owner-occupied home: $227,600.
  • Median monthly cost with a mortgage: $1,626, and $640 without.
  • Median gross rent: $972.
  • Median household income: $74,216 in 2024 dollars.
  • Housing units, July 2025: 58,780.
  • Building permits in 2025: 163.

sections.h2: How much did the 2026 triennial update change Wood County values?
sections.html:
Residential values rose by an average of 19 percent countywide in the 2026 triennial update, according to the Auditor's press release. Ohio requires a full reappraisal every six years, and Wood County did its reappraisal in 2023, so 2026 brought the mid-cycle update by neighborhood.

The update applies to tax year 2026, payable in February and July 2027, with a lien date of January 1, 2026. Values are set statistically from arm's length sales of the prior three years, so one parcel can land above or below the average depending on location and condition.

The Auditor adds that a value jump does not carry through to the bill at the same rate. House Bill 920 reduces voted outside millage as values grow, House Bill 186 adds an inflation cap credit for school districts, and House Bill 335 applies a similar cap to inside millage. Inside millage is the unvoted portion that cannot exceed 10 mills in a taxing district. Renewal levies keep the current millage, a renewal with an increase raises it, and an additional levy is a new tax.

sections.h2: When are Wood County property taxes due, and where can you pay?
sections.html:
Real estate and manufactured home taxes are due in February and July, and the Treasurer sets the exact dates each year. The Treasurer's office says there are roughly 80 taxing districts in the county, each with its own rate. A payment received after the due date draws a 5 percent penalty for the first 10 days and 10 percent after that, as the Treasurer's information page cites it.

Ohio law relies on the postmark for mailed payments, and the Treasurer warns that a postmark may show the day a machine processed the envelope, not the day you dropped it off. Mail early, or ask the post office for a hand-stamped postmark. Questions go to 419-354-9130.

sections.h2: How do you appeal a Wood County valuation?
sections.html:
The formal route is a Board of Revision complaint, filed with the Auditor between January 1 and March 31. For the 2026 triennial update, the Auditor's FAQ gives March 31, 2027 as the last day. Before going formal, an owner may ask for an informal review.

  • Evidence for an informal review: an appraisal less than two years old, three or more comparable sales from 2023 to 2025, or a sales listing.
  • The FAQ says a dispute over more than $50,000 must go to the Board of Revision.
  • The Auditor's site offers a Sales List, a Sales Search and a Comp Search, and the Comp Search is described as the most useful.
  • Under R.C. 5715.19, only one complaint is allowed per interim period unless a sale, casualty, major improvement or occupancy change occurred after the lien date.

The real estate office takes calls at 419-354-9173 and sits on the second floor of the county office building.

sections.h2: Which Wood County tax reduction programs apply to a house?
sections.html:
The Auditor's tax reduction page lists four programs that touch a typical home or small farm.

  • Homestead exemption for owners 65 or older, or permanently and totally disabled. The page states a modified adjusted gross income limit of $40,000 for late applicants on tax year 2025 and $41,000 for new applicants on tax year 2026. The home must be the primary residence.
  • Disabled veteran homestead exemption, for qualified veterans or a surviving spouse.
  • Owner occupied reduction, which needs an application and applies to a home the owner lives in.
  • Agricultural use valuation for 10 or more acres in farming, with a $25.00 fee for new applications and a penalty if the land is sold and drops below 10 acres or leaves farming.

An agricultural district application is free and shields farmland from some water and sewer assessments. Call 419-354-9167 for homestead questions and 419-354-9174 for agricultural programs.

sections.h2: What fees come up when you sell in Wood County?
sections.html:
Wood County charges a conveyance fee of $3.00 per $1,000 of the purchase price, with the price rounded up to the nearest hundred, plus a $0.50 per parcel transfer fee. The Auditor points to form DTE 100(EX) for deeds that qualify for an exemption.

The grantee files a statement of value before the Auditor endorses the deed, and R.C. 319.202 makes the grantor responsible for the conveyance fee. It also requires disclosure when the parcel has farm valuation that could trigger a recoupment charge. Sheriff sales are listed on the Auditor's real estate page, which is worth a look if a property has fallen behind on taxes.

Ask the Treasurer for a current balance before you sign a contract, and ask the Auditor whether any special assessment is pending on the parcel. The Auditor posts a pending special assessments file for 2026 on its real estate page.

faqs.q: When are Wood County property taxes due?
faqs.a: In February and July. The Treasurer sets the exact dates each year, and late payments carry a 5 percent penalty in the first 10 days and 10 percent after that.

faqs.q: How much did Wood County home values rise in 2026?
faqs.a: The Auditor reports an average residential increase of 19 percent from the 2026 triennial update. Individual parcels vary by neighborhood, and tax bills do not rise at the same rate because of House Bills 920, 186 and 335.

faqs.q: What is the Wood County deadline to file a Board of Revision complaint?
faqs.a: March 31, with the Auditor's FAQ naming March 31, 2027 for the 2026 tax year. The filing window opens January 1.

faqs.q: What is the Wood County conveyance fee?
faqs.a: $3.00 per $1,000 of the purchase price, rounded up to the nearest hundred, plus a $0.50 transfer fee per parcel, as the Auditor's FAQ states.

faqs.q: Who do I call about Wood County property taxes?
faqs.a: Call the Treasurer at 419-354-9130 for payment and bill questions, and the Auditor's real estate office at 419-354-9173 for values. The toll free line is 866-860-4140.
